questions.scenario: During the construction of a 4-level basement for an institutional complex, the RGBC's site team discovers that a major reinforced concrete retaining wall has been poured with concrete containing an excessive water-cement ratio, resulting in severe honeycombing and compressive core test results far below the approved design strength. The Authorized Person (AP) requests the RGBC to keep the issue internal while formulating a localized cosmetic grouting method statement without notifying the Building Authority (BA). How must the RGBC Authorized Signatory (AS) legally act under the Buildings Ordinance?
options: A. Comply with the AP's direction, since the AP is the lead professional holding statutory authority over the site supervisory team and design amendments under Section 4.

B. Issue an immediate written report to the BA detailing the defective materials and work, as Section 9(5)(b) imposes an independent statutory duty on the registered contractor to report material defects to the BA regardless of the AP's instructions.
C. Proceed with the cosmetic patch repair immediately and submit an as-built structural amendment on Specified Form BA14 upon final completion of all substructure works.
D. Submit a formal suspension notice under Form BA10 within 7 days and cease all site operations until the Structural Engineer (RSE) resubmits structural calculations.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 9(5)(b) & Section 40(2A)(b)
questions.rationale: Under Section 9(5)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), every registered contractor shall give written notice to the Building Authority if it comes to their knowledge that any work has been or is being carried out in contravention of the Ordinance or in material divergence from approved plans, or if defective materials are used. An instruction from the AP or RSE does not relieve the RGBC AS from this statutory reporting duty; failure to report constitutes a criminal offense under Section 40(2A)(b).

questions.scenario: The Building Authority granted consent under Section 16(1)(b) for deep excavation and lateral support (ELS) works subject to a specific condition under Section 17(1) requiring pre-grouting and real-time groundwater drawdown monitoring at designated boundary piezometers before advancing excavation below -5.0 mPD. Facing project delays, the RGBC AS directs the excavation team to dig to -8.5 mPD before installing the piezometers, claiming the ground is predominantly solid granite and stable. What statutory liability applies directly to the RGBC AS?
options: A. The RGBC AS is subject only to an administrative warning letter and a geotechnical audit from the Geotechnical Engineering Office (GEO).

B. The AS has committed a strict liability offense under Section 40(2AA) for failing to comply with a condition imposed under Section 17(1), liable on conviction to a fine of $250,000 and 2 years imprisonment.
C. The AS is exempt from liability if the RSE subsequently verifies by retrospective finite element calculation that ground settlement remained under 10 mm.
D. The Building Authority may only deduct performance points under the Contractor Management Handbook without criminal prosecution.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 17(1) & Section 40(2AA)
questions.rationale: Section 17(1) empowers the Building Authority to impose conditions when granting approval or consent. Section 40(2AA) explicitly provides that any person who fails to comply with any condition imposed under Section 17(1) shall be guilty of an offense and liable on conviction to a fine of HK$250,000 and to imprisonment for 2 years. It is a direct statutory penal provision and cannot be remedied post hoc by engineer calculations.

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained consent to commence superstructure works on 15 January. Due to contractual disputes over curtain wall subcontracting, no physical building works commence on site. On 20 April of the same year, the client settles the dispute and instructs the RGBC to cast the first batch of columns immediately using the existing consent. How should the RGBC AS evaluate the statutory status of the consent?
options: A. The consent is still valid because building consents under Cap. 123 remain automatically active for 12 months from the date of grant.

B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) because works were not commenced within 3 months of the grant; the RGBC must apply for renewal under Section 20(2) on Form BA9 and obtain approval before commencing.
C. The RGBC may commence immediately provided that a supplementary Form BA10 commencement notification is served to the BA at least 24 hours prior to concreting.
D. The consent has expired, requiring the AP to re-submit all superstructure architectural and structural plans for full 60-day plan approval under Section 14(1).
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & Section 20(2); B(A)R Regulation 34 & Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, a consent is deemed to be revoked if the works for which it was given are not commenced within 3 months of the date of the consent (15 January to 15 April exceeds 3 months). Commencing works under a revoked consent constitutes carrying out works without consent under Section 14(1), an offense under Section 40(1AA)/40(2A). The contractor must apply for renewal under Section 20(2) using Specified Form BA9 pursuant to B(A)R Regulation 34 and wait for renewal before commencing.

questions.scenario: An RGBC has substantially completed an 18-storey industrial conversion project. During the joint final inspection for an Occupation Permit (OP), the Building Authority discovers that the final constructed width of the ground-floor exit corridors connecting to the ultimate place of safety is 1.05m instead of the 1.60m specified on the approved building plans, severely compromising fire exit capacity. Under which statutory ground may the Building Authority refuse to issue the OP?
options: A. Section 21(6)(a), because the building owner has not discharged all outstanding rates and government land rent liabilities.
B. Section 21(6)(d), because the building works have resulted in material divergence from the approved plan or contravene a provision of the Buildings Ordinance or its subsidiary regulations.
C. Section 21(6)(b), because the Authorized Person failed to provide three months advance written notice of intended completion.
D. Section 21(8), because an occupation permit cannot be refused if practical completion has been certified by the contract administrator.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 21(6)(d)
questions.rationale: Section 21(6)(d) of the Buildings Ordinance stipulates that the Building Authority may refuse to issue a temporary occupation permit or an occupation permit if the building works have resulted in material divergence from the approved plan or contravene any provision of the Ordinance or its regulations (such as fire safety exit route requirements under B(P)R). A reduction of corridor width from 1.6m to 1.05m is a direct material divergence and life-safety contravention.

questions.scenario: During ongoing caisson and trench works, a water main bursts, washing out subterranean fines. The BA inspects the site and finds that adjacent tenement buildings exhibit rapidly widening diagonal masonry cracks and bulging retaining structures, creating imminent danger to life. Under which section does the BA have the express statutory power to issue a Cease Works Order and enter adjacent premises to execute emergency stabilizing works?
options: A. Section 23, empowering the BA to order the cessation of building works being carried out in a dangerous manner, and Section 26/26A for dangerous buildings.
B. Section 16(1), by issuing an immediate retroactive rejection of structural drawings.
C. Section 30, requiring the RGBC to appoint an independent Registered Geotechnical Engineer within 28 days.
D. Section 13, authorizing the disciplinary board to inspect structural safety on site.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 23(1) & (2)
questions.rationale: Under Section 23(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, where in the opinion of the Building Authority any building works or street works are being carried out in such a manner as to cause, or will be likely to cause, a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property, the BA may by order in writing served on the registered contractor or the AP order the immediate cessation of such works. Section 23(2) and Section 26 allow the BA to carry out emergency works to eliminate the danger at the owner's/contractor's expense.

questions.scenario: An RGBC carrying out alteration works on an existing commercial building constructs an unapproved external structural steel cantilevered canopy over a busy public pedestrian pavement. The BA issues an order under Section 24(1) requiring demolition and removal of the unauthorized building works within 30 days. The building owner instructs the RGBC not to comply, claiming that an appeal to the Town Planning Board has been lodged. If the RGBC refuses to pull down the canopy as ordered, what direct statutory enforcement consequence applies under Cap. 123?
options: A. The order is automatically stayed until all town planning administrative appeals are fully exhausted.

B. Under Section 24(3), the Building Authority may demolish or remove the works using government contractors and recover the full cost of the works plus a surcharge under Section 33, while the non-compliant party faces criminal prosecution under Section 40(1BA).
C. The BA must convert the Section 24 order into a civil writ of injunction before taking any physical demolition action.
D. The canopy will automatically be granted a temporary retention permit under the Minor Works Validation Scheme.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 24(1), Section 24(3) & Section 33
questions.rationale: Under Section 24(3) of the Buildings Ordinance, if an order served under Section 24(1) is not complied with within the specified time, the Building Authority may cause the unauthorized works to be demolished, removed, or altered as necessary. Under Section 33, the expenses incurred by the BA together with a surcharge (up to 20%) are recoverable from the person upon whom the order was served. Non-compliance with a Section 24 order is an offense under Section 40(1BA).

questions.scenario: Deep excavation adjacent to a pre-war 4-storey unreinforced masonry building causes rapid differential settlement of 65 mm. The BA determines under Section 24A that the building is in a dangerous condition, posing an imminent risk of structural collapse onto the occupants. What specific statutory power does Section 24A grant to the Building Authority in this emergency?
options: A. The BA may make an application to the District Court for an immediate Closure Order to close the building and evict all occupants without prior notice.
B. The BA may serve a 6-month statutory investigation notice requiring the landlord to carry out non-destructive testing.
C. The BA can only erect exterior protective hoardings and must await a full tribunal hearing under the Landlord and Tenant (Consolidation) Ordinance.
D. The BA must order the AP to redesign the foundation of the neighboring building within 14 days.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 24A(1) & (2)
questions.rationale: Under Section 24A of the Buildings Ordinance, where the Building Authority considers that a building is in a dangerous condition or is likely to become dangerous, the BA may apply to the District Court for a Closure Order to close the building and enable necessary works to be carried out or to prevent danger to life. Under Section 24A(2), in situations of imminent danger, the court may make an interim closure order immediately.

questions.scenario: An RGBC's Authorized Signatory signs and submits a statutory certification on Specified Form BA14 declaring that all structural reinforced concrete works for a multi-storey development have been executed in strict compliance with the approved structural drawings. In reality, the AS knew that the site team deliberately omitted 40% of the shear link reinforcement in 12 major transfer columns to save cost. What is the maximum statutory penalty that the AS faces personally under Section 40(1AA)?
options: A. A fine of HK$100,000 and 6 months imprisonment.
B. A fine of HK$250,000 and 1 year imprisonment.
C. A fine of HK$500,000 and 3 years imprisonment.
D. A fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years imprisonment.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 40(1AA)
questions.rationale: Section 40(1AA) of the Buildings Ordinance provides that any person who knowingly misrepresents a material fact in any plan, certificate, form, report, notice or other document given to the Building Authority commits an offense. The statutory penalty prescribed under Section 40(1AA) is a fine of HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years.

questions.scenario: To fast-track construction, an RGBC AS instructs the site manager to dismantle critical falsework and heavy shoring beneath a freshly cast 2.5m thick transfer plate just 4 days after concreting, far ahead of the approved 28-day curing and back-propping sequence shown in the approved method statement. The transfer plate sags severely, causing sudden progressive shear failure and crushing two mobile cranes below, resulting in severe physical injuries to 3 workers. Under which statutory provision is the RGBC directly liable to criminal prosecution?
options: A. Section 40(2B)(b), carrying a maximum fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years imprisonment for carrying out works in a manner likely to cause a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property.
B. Section 40(1), carrying a fixed fine of HK$2,000 for non-compliance with routine general administration.
C. Section 40(2A), limited strictly to a civil penalty assessed by the Construction Industry Council.
D. Section 13(4), which empowers the Magistrates' Court to impose a 5-year custodial sentence under professional disciplinary procedures.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 40(2B)(b)
questions.rationale: Under Section 40(2B)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance, any person directly concerned with the carrying out of any building works or street works who carries out such works, or causes them to be carried out, in such a manner as to cause, or to be likely to cause, a risk of injury to any person or damage to any property, commits an offense. The penalty is a fine of HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years.

questions.scenario: Following an RGBC's conviction in the Magistrates' Court under Section 40(2A)(b) for carrying out structural building works in material divergence from approved plans, the Building Authority refers the matter to a Disciplinary Board constituted under Section 13 of the Buildings Ordinance. What statutory orders is the Disciplinary Board legally empowered to make against the registered contractor?
options: A. Impose a 2-year custodial prison sentence on the Authorized Signatory and confiscate the contractor's corporate bank accounts.
B. Order that the contractor's name be removed from the register permanently or for a period, or fine the contractor up to HK$250,000, and/or reprimand the contractor.
C. Order the contractor to pay punitive damages directly to the project developer under civil tort law.
D. Direct the Hong Kong Police Force to impound all plant and machinery registered in the company name.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 13(4) & (4A)
questions.rationale: Under Section 13(4) and (4A) of the Buildings Ordinance, a Disciplinary Board, upon hearing charges against a registered contractor, may order: (a) that the contractor be reprimanded; (b) that the contractor's name be removed from the register (either permanently or for such period as the board thinks fit); or (c) that the contractor be fined a sum not exceeding HK$250,000. Disciplinary boards are administrative/quasi-judicial tribunals and have NO statutory power to impose custodial sentences (prison) or order civil damages.

questions.scenario: A client decides to replace the structural steelwork Registered Specialist Contractor (RSC) on an active commercial tower project with a newly qualified RSC. Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8 and Specified Form BA8, how must the appointment of the new contractor and notification of termination of the outgoing contractor be statutorily handled?
options: A. The Authorized Person (AP) submits Form BA8 within 14 days after the new RSC commences work on site.

B. The person for whom the building works are being carried out must notify the Building Authority in the specified form (Form BA8) of the appointment of the new RSC and the termination of the former contractor's appointment within 7 days of such appointment.
C. The new RSC submits Form BA8 jointly with the outgoing RSC within 28 days of the contract assignment.
D. The outgoing contractor must submit Form BA8 within 48 hours, failing which the new contractor cannot be formally recognized.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1) & (2); Specified Form BA8
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1) & (2), if a registered contractor ceases to be appointed, the person for whom the works are being carried out must notify the Building Authority in the specified form (Form BA8) within 7 days of the appointment of a new contractor, giving the new contractor's name and registration details and stating the cessation of the former contractor's appointment. Notice is not submitted post-commencement nor by the AP alone.

questions.scenario: An RGBC was granted consent under Section 16(1)(b) to construct an institutional building on 1 March. Due to financing delays, site work cannot commence by 31 May. What is the statutory status of the consent under Section 20 of the Buildings Ordinance, and how should the RGBC and AP proceed using Form BA9?
options: A. The consent remains valid indefinitely provided the Authorized Person submits a letter of explanation before the building reaches physical completion.

B. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) because works did not commence within 3 months; the AP must apply for consent renewal using Specified Form BA9 under Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34.
C. The consent is automatically extended for another 6 months upon payment of the prescribed administrative fee without any form submission.
D. Under B(A)R Regulation 27, the Building Authority suspends the consent for 12 months.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & (2); Building (Administration) Regulation 34; Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 20(1), a consent to commence building works is deemed revoked if the works are not commenced within 3 months from the date of the consent. Under Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34, the consent may be renewed upon application in the specified form (Form BA9) submitted by the AP/RSE. Citing repealed B(A)R Regulation 27 is incorrect.

questions.scenario: An RGBC holding an approved consent for demolition works intends to commence on-site demolition operations on Monday, 18 September. Under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) and Specified Form BA10, by what latest date must the RGBC ensure the notice of commencement is formally received by the Building Authority?
options: A. 17 September (at least 24 hours prior to commencement)
B. 11 September (not less than 7 days prior to commencement)
C. 4 September (not less than 14 days prior to commencement)
D. 18 September, provided notice is delivered by hand on the morning of commencement
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1); Specified Form BA10
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) explicitly requires that a registered contractor must give notice of intended commencement on Specified Form BA10 to the Building Authority not less than 7 days before the day on which the building works are commenced. For commencement on 18 September, the notice must be received no later than 11 September.

questions.scenario: A 25-storey commercial office development has reached physical completion. The developer wishes to apply for an Occupation Permit under BO Section 21. Which combination of statutory forms must be submitted to the Building Authority by the AP and RGBC to effectuate this application?
options: A. Form BA10 submitted by the RGBC and Form BA9 submitted by the AP.
B. Form BA12 (Application for temporary occupation permit) submitted by the Registered Structural Engineer only.
C. Form BA13 (Application for Occupation Permit) submitted by the AP, accompanied by Form BA14 (Certificate of completion of building works) signed by the RGBC's Authorized Signatory.
D. Form MW05 submitted jointly by the RGBC and Registered Safety Officer.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 21; Building (Administration) Regulations 25(1) & 33; Specified Forms BA13 & BA14
questions.rationale: An application for an Occupation Permit under BO Section 21 is submitted by the AP using Specified Form BA13 pursuant to B(A)R Regulation 33. Under B(A)R Regulation 25(1), the application must be accompanied by a completion certificate on Specified Form BA14 duly signed by the RGBC's Authorized Signatory (and RSE/AP where applicable) certifying that the works have been executed in accordance with the Ordinance and approved plans.

questions.scenario: On a complex commercial shopping complex, specialized ventilation works and fire service installations were executed by a Registered Specialist Contractor (Ventilation Category). When the AP submits the application for an Occupation Permit on Form BA13, which completion certificate must be submitted specifically by the RSC under B(A)R Regulation 25(2)?
options: A. Form BA14A signed by the Registered Specialist Contractor's Authorized Signatory.
B. Form BA14 signed solely by the main contractor's Registered Structural Engineer.
C. Form MW02 signed by the Prescribed Registered Contractor.
D. Form BA8 signed jointly by the Building Authority and Fire Services Department.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 25(2); Specified Form BA14A
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 25(2) mandates that where specialized works are carried out by a Registered Specialist Contractor (RSC), the application for an Occupation Permit or certificate of completion must include Specified Form BA14A signed by the RSC's Authorized Signatory certifying the completion of those specialized works in accordance with the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: A commercial building owner commissions an RGBC to carry out Class I Minor Works involving the alteration of external wall finishes higher than 3m. Before commencing works and upon completion, which prescribed forms under the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) must be submitted to the Building Authority?
options: A. Form BA10 at least 7 days before commencement, and Form BA14 within 14 days after completion.
B. Form MW01 at least 7 days before commencement, and Form MW02 within 14 days after completion, both prepared with the appointed Prescribed Building Professional (AP/RSE).
C. Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencement, and Form MW04 within 28 days after completion.
D. Form MW05 within 14 days after completion, with no prior notice required.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 27, 28 & 29; Specified Forms MW01 & MW02
questions.rationale: Under the simplified requirements of the Minor Works Control System (Cap. 123N), Class I minor works require the appointment of a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) and a Prescribed Registered Contractor (PRC). Form MW01 (Notice of commencement with plans) must be submitted not less than 7 days before commencement (Sections 27-28), and Form MW02 (Certificate of completion) must be submitted within 14 days after completion (Section 29).

questions.scenario: An RGBC is appointed directly by an owners' corporation to carry out a Class II minor works item (repair of an external structural frame without structural alteration) where no Prescribed Building Professional (AP/RSE) is statutorily required. Under B(MW)R Sections 30 and 32, which forms and timelines govern this work?
options: A. Form MW01 not less than 7 days prior to commencement; Form MW02 within 7 days of completion.
B. Form MW03 not less than 7 days prior to commencement; Form MW04 within 14 days of completion.
C. Form MW05 within 14 days after completion; no prior commencement notice is needed.
D. Form BA10 not less than 7 days prior to commencement; Form BA14 within 14 days of completion.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 30 & 32; Specified Forms MW03 & MW04
questions.rationale: Under Cap. 123N Sections 30 and 32, for Class II minor works where no Prescribed Building Professional is appointed, the Prescribed Registered Contractor (RGBC/RMWC) must submit Form MW03 (Notice of commencement accompanied by plans/sketches) not less than 7 days before commencement, and submit Form MW04 (Certificate of completion accompanied by photos) within 14 days after completion.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is engaged by a domestic unit owner to carry out Class III Minor Works (erection of an air-conditioning support metal frame projecting less than 600mm from an external wall). What are the statutory filing requirements under Section 35 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N)?
options: A. Submit Form MW03 at least 7 days prior to commencement and Form MW04 upon completion.
B. No prior notice is required before commencement; the RGBC must submit Form MW05 along with photos of the completed work within 14 days after completion.
C. Submit Form MW01 with structural calculations 7 days before commencement and Form MW02 within 28 days of completion.
D. Class III works are fully exempted works under BO Section 41(1) and do not require any form submission to the Building Authority.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 35; Specified Form MW05
questions.rationale: Under B(MW)R Section 35, Class III minor works do not require prior notice of commencement. The appointed contractor (PRC) must submit notice of completion on Specified Form MW05, together with photographs showing the condition of the works before and after completion, within 14 days after the date of completion of the works. They are designated minor works under Cap. 123N, not Section 41(1) exempted works.

questions.scenario: A client appoints an RGBC to carry out a combination of Class II minor works where a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) is voluntarily appointed to design and supervise the works. Under B(MW)R Section 31 and Section 33, which forms must be submitted to the Building Authority?
options: A. Form MW03 before commencement and Form MW04 after completion.
B. Form MW01 not less than 7 days before commencement, and Form MW06 within 14 days after completion.
C. Form MW03 not less than 7 days before commencement, and Form MW06 within 14 days after completion.
D. Form BA10 before commencement and Form BA14 after completion.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 31 & 33; Specified Forms MW01 & MW06
questions.rationale: Under B(MW)R Section 31, if a Prescribed Building Professional is appointed for Class II minor works, Form MW01 must be submitted not less than 7 days before commencement (incorporating the PBP certification and plans). Under Section 33, upon completion of such Class II works involving a PBP, Form MW06 is the prescribed completion certificate submitted jointly by the PBP and PRC within 14 days.

questions.scenario: A property owner intends to carry out an alteration that creates a 2.5m-wide opening in a non-load-bearing masonry partition wall inside an office unit. The RGBC advises that this is a Class II Minor Works item under Schedule 1 of Cap. 123N. However, upon reviewing the structural drawings, the RGBC discovers the wall is actually a designated reinforced concrete shear wall (load-bearing). If the RGBC executes the opening under the Minor Works Control System using Form MW03, what statutory breach occurs?
options: A. None, because minor cutting of structural walls is allowable under Class I Minor Works using Form MW01.

B. The work cannot fall under the Minor Works Control System as structural alterations to load-bearing walls require prior plan approval and formal consent under Section 14(1) of the Buildings Ordinance; proceeding under MWCS constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A).
C. The contractor only needs to pay a 10% penalty fee and submit Form MW05 after completion.
D. The works are exempt under Section 41(3) provided they are completed within 7 calendar days.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 14(1), Section 40(2A); Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Schedule 1
questions.rationale: Under Schedule 1 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), minor works items strictly exclude alterations to load-bearing structural elements (such as RC shear walls) unless explicitly specified under stringent prescribed criteria (which do not allow arbitrary 2.5m openings). Structural alterations to load-bearing walls require prior approval of plans and consent under BO Section 14(1). Commencing such works under MWCS forms constitutes carrying out unauthorized building works without approval/consent, an offence under BO Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: During an unexpected site inspection by the Buildings Department on an active 24-storey commercial redevelopment, the RGBC's site agent is unable to produce the Building Authority's approved structural framing drawings or the certified site supervision plan, explaining that the master sets are maintained at the contractor's headquarters across the harbour to prevent damage. The site agent offers digital PDF copies on a tablet instead.
options: A. The RGBC is compliant because digital electronic copies of approved plans are statutorily recognized as equivalent to paper site copies under the Electronic Transactions Ordinance.

B. The RGBC is in breach of Building (Administration) Regulation 10, which mandates that the copy of approved plans and supervisory documents returned by the Building Authority must be kept on site at all times during the progress of works.
C. The site agent can avoid liability by producing the documents at the local Buildings Department office within 48 hours of the inspection.
D. Keeping approved plans off-site is legally permitted provided the Project Authorized Person has certified an off-site document control protocol.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 10 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2B)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 10, the registered contractor must keep the copy of approved plans and documents returned to him or the Authorized Person on the site of the building works at all times during the execution of the works. Failure to comply with this requirement without reasonable excuse constitutes a statutory offence under Section 40(2B) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: Four months following the issuance of an Occupation Permit for a residential tower, an RGBC clears its central project archives and permanently shreds all original batching plant delivery tickets, concrete cube crushing reports, and Site Safety Supervision Plan daily inspection logs. Seven months later, the Buildings Department initiates an audit into concrete strength variability on the project.
options: A. The contractor is fully compliant because statutory document retention obligations terminate automatically upon the issuance of the Occupation Permit under Section 21.
B. The contractor is legally protected provided summary test graphs were counter-signed by the Registered Structural Engineer before disposal.

C. The contractor has committed an offence under Building (Administration) Regulation 11 for failing to retain all testing records and supervisory logs for not less than 12 months after practical completion or issuance of the occupation permit.
D. The contractor is only required to retain mill certificates for structural steelwork, while concrete cube logs are the sole custody responsibility of the testing laboratory.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 11 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 11 explicitly obliges registered contractors to keep and preserve all records of tests on materials, plant, and structural elements, as well as site supervision logbooks, for a minimum period of not less than 12 months from the date of completion of the works or the grant of an occupation permit. Destroying these records at 4 months post-OP violates Regulation 11 and constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: An RGBC receives written consent to commence deep basement excavation on Monday, 3 August. Anxious to avoid contractual liquidated damages, the Authorized Signatory submits Specified Form BA10 (Notice of Commencement) via the BD electronic system on Thursday, 6 August, stating that excavation works will commence on Monday, 10 August, and immediately mobilizes excavators onto site on 10 August.
options: A. The commencement notice is legally valid because 4 calendar days are statutorily sufficient if the Building Authority does not issue an objection.

B. The commencement is unlawful under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), which requires that the notice of commencement on Form BA10 be served on the Building Authority not less than 7 days prior to the date on which works are to begin.
C. The RGBC may commence after 48 hours provided the Authorized Person and Registered Geotechnical Engineer have co-signed the Form BA10.
D. Form BA10 is an advisory administrative document and failure to observe the 7-day window carries no statutory liability under Section 40(2A).
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 20(1) & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) specifies that a registered contractor must give to the Building Authority not less than 7 days' prior notice in the specified form (Form BA10) of the date on which building works are to be commenced. Serving notice on 6 August for a 10 August commencement gives only 4 days' notice, breaching Regulation 20(1) and exposing the contractor to prosecution under Section 40(2A) of the Buildings Ordinance.

questions.scenario: During the erection and pre-stressing of heavy structural steel trusses on a sports facility, the RGBC's sole Authorized Signatory travels overseas for three weeks without delegating statutory oversight to an approved competent supervisor, leaving only an unregistered trade subcontractor to oversee the critical tensioning operations.
options: A. The RGBC satisfies continuous supervision requirements as long as the sub-contractor holds a general trade competency certificate from the Construction Industry Council.

B. The RGBC is in breach of Building (Administration) Regulation 26 and Section 9(5)(a) of the Buildings Ordinance, which require continuous supervision of building works by the registered contractor.
C. The absence of the Authorized Signatory is legally immaterial if the Registered Structural Engineer's TCP T5 was present during the prestressing pour.
D. Continuous supervision under Regulation 26 applies solely to foundation socketing and deep compaction, not to superstructure steel erection.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A) Regulation 26 & Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5)(a)
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 26 imposes a mandatory duty on every registered contractor carrying out building works to give continuous supervision to the works. This directly reinforces Section 9(5)(a) of the Buildings Ordinance. Abandoning site supervision during critical structural operations without authorized, competent cover breaches Regulation 26 and Section 9(5)(a), rendering the contractor liable to disciplinary action and criminal prosecution.

questions.scenario: An RGBC was granted consent under Section 16(1)(b) to commence site formation works on 15 January. Due to a prolonged contractual dispute, the RGBC did not commence any works on site. On 20 April (exceeding 3 months from consent), the developer instructs the RGBC to start earthmoving immediately without seeking further authorization from the Building Authority.
options: A. The consent remains valid because building consents are effective for 12 months from the date of issue.

B. The consent has expired under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, and the RGBC must apply for renewal on Form BA9, with commencement prohibited until the renewed consent is endorsed under B(A)R Regulation 34.
C. The RGBC can commence immediately provided a revised Form BA10 is served with at least 7 days' notice.
D. Under Section 20(2), consent renewal is purely automatic upon paying the prescribed administrative re-application fee.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & (2); Building (Administration) Regulations Regulation 34 & Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, a consent to commence building works expires if the works are not commenced within 3 months from the date of the consent. To reactivate the consent, an application for renewal must be submitted on Form BA9 under Section 20(2), and under B(A)R Regulation 34, the renewed consent must be endorsed on the notice of consent before works can lawfully proceed.

questions.scenario: To accommodate site management and sub-contractor personnel, an RGBC erects a 3-storey temporary building consisting of stacked steel shipping containers with a height of 8.5m on the building site without applying for a temporary building permit or obtaining approval from the Building Authority.
options: A. Temporary container offices on active construction sites are fully exempt from all provisions of the Building (Planning) Regulations regardless of height or usage.

B. The structure breaches Building (Planning) Regulations Part IX (Regulations 53 to 55), as any temporary contractor shed or office exceeding 2 storeys or 6m in height requires prior written permission and must comply with structural stability and fire separation rules.
C. Container offices are governed solely by the Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance and do not fall within the definition of building works under Section 2 of the Buildings Ordinance.
D. The contractor is exempt if the containers are supported on timber blocks rather than a permanent cast-in-place concrete ground slab.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Planning) Regulations (Cap. 123F) Part IX (Regulations 53, 54 & 55) & Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1)
questions.rationale: Under Building (Planning) Regulations Part IX (specifically Regulations 53 to 55), temporary contractor sheds and buildings on site that exceed single-storey limits or specified dimensional ceilings (such as 2 storeys / 6m) require written permission from the Building Authority and must satisfy stringent fire and structural requirements. Erecting a 3-storey container complex without authorization constitutes unauthorized building works under Section 14(1) and violates Part IX of the B(P)R.

questions.scenario: To construct an external hoarding with an integrated covered public walkway fronting a congested urban roadway, the RGBC designs the covered walkway with a clear internal headroom of 2.1m and an internal clear pedestrian width of 0.9m between the protective handrails and the external fence.
options: A. The dimensions are acceptable provided reflective hazard tape and emergency battery lighting are installed along the ceiling soffit.

B. The dimensions violate PNRC 4 (Appendix A), which mandates that covered walkways along public streets must maintain a minimum clear headroom of not less than 2.5m and a minimum clear walking width of not less than 1.1m.
C. The minimum clear width required by PNRC 4 is 0.8m, so the 0.9m width is compliant while only the headroom is non-compliant.
D. Hoarding and walkway dimensions are determined entirely at the discretion of the Authorized Person without statutory or practice note minimums.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 4 (Appendix A) & Building (Planning) Regulations Regulation 49
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 4 (Appendix A) and Building (Planning) Regulation 49, temporary covered walkways erected over or adjoining public footpaths must satisfy prescribed physical clearances: the clear internal height (headroom) must not be less than 2.5m, and the clear walkway width for pedestrian movement must not be less than 1.1m. Both dimensions in the scenario violate these statutory practice standards.

questions.scenario: During pipe-jacking operations executed within the Railway Protection Zone of an underground MTR tunnel, the RGBC's instrumentation array records an accumulated ground settlement of 21mm directly above the running tunnel crown, exceeding the pre-established Alert Level of 20mm.
options: A. The RGBC may continue pipe jacking at normal rates until the settlement exceeds the 25mm Action Level.

B. Pursuant to PNRC 14 (PNAP APP-24), the RGBC must immediately inform the MTRCL and the Buildings Department, review the excavation method, and implement predetermined protective measures before settlement escalates to the Alarm/Action thresholds.
C. The RGBC is only required to log the reading in the Site Safety Supervision Plan diary at the end of the weekly shift.
D. Trigger levels within railway protection zones apply exclusively to deep diaphragm walling and not to pipe-jacking or micro-tunnelling works.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 14 (APP-24) & Buildings Ordinance Section 17(1)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 14 (PNAP APP-24), the Railway Protection Zone monitoring framework establishes Alert, Alarm, and Action limits (with Alert commonly set at 20mm or as agreed with MTRCL). When an Alert level is triggered, the contractor must immediately notify the BD and MTRCL, initiate an immediate technical review of the construction sequence, and adopt proactive ground-stabilizing measures to prevent reaching the structural safety threshold.

questions.scenario: A specialist piling company registered as an RGBC has only one approved Authorized Signatory (AS) on the Buildings Department register. Following a corporate restructuring, this sole AS tenders his immediate resignation and departs the company while foundation bored piling is actively proceeding on site. The RGBC's Managing Director instructs the site to proceed under the direction of an experienced Project Director who is not an approved AS.
options: A. The RGBC can lawfully continue piling operations for up to 90 days while preparing an application for a replacement AS.

B. Pursuant to PNRC 38 Section 4 and Section 9(5) of the Buildings Ordinance, the RGBC must cease all building works forthwith and cannot carry out any works until a replacement Authorized Signatory is formally approved by the Building Authority.
C. Piling may continue uninterrupted provided the Registered Geotechnical Engineer's TCP T4 signs daily safety clearances.
D. The RGBC may appoint an external Authorized Signatory from an affiliated joint-venture partner via a board resolution without prior BD vetting.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 38 Section 4 & Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5), 9(6)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 38, if an RGBC ceases to have any approved Authorized Signatory to act on its behalf, the contractor no longer meets the statutory registration criteria under Section 9(5) & 9(6) of the Buildings Ordinance. The RGBC must immediately cease all building works on all active sites forthwith. Continuing works without an approved AS constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: On a site involving deep excavation and lateral support adjoining sensitive buildings, the RGBC's designated Contractor Stream Technically Competent Person Grade T3 (TCP T3) is also concurrently appointed by the project developer as the AP/RSE Stream TCP T3 to save supervisory costs.
options: A. Dual appointment across streams is permitted under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision provided the individual holds a recognized chartered engineering qualification.
B. The appointment is invalid because the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision strictly prohibits cross-stream concurrent appointments between the Contractor Stream and the AP/RSE/RGE Stream.
C. Cross-stream concurrent appointments are allowed if the total site area does not exceed 1,000 square metres.
D. The concurrent appointment requires only the written consent of the Registered Geotechnical Engineer logged into the site diary.
questions.statutoryRef: Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) Section 5 & PNRC 38
questions.rationale: Under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) Section 5, site safety supervision is divided into distinct, independent functional streams (the AP/RSE/RGE stream for design compliance verification and the Contractor stream for construction execution quality/safety). To avoid conflicts of interest, a TCP is strictly prohibited from concurrently undertaking safety supervision responsibilities across different functional streams on the same project.
